findings.description: PASS, and the r3 blocker is genuinely closed. Every row of the per-case baseline table was re-derived by executing the rendered baseline scripts against failing stubs, and every row now matches measurement. The three `one failure does not stop the rest` rows correctly read `pass`: continuation already works at all three multi-call sites, exactly as the clause now says. The 15-case arithmetic (4+4+3+4) is right, the case titles are derivable from the Measured baseline table, and every case is constructible under a scrubbed PATH.
findings.evidence: Executed at 1dec91c on this machine, PATH scrubbed to a stub dir plus /usr/bin:/bin, synthetic HOME: rendered install-vscode-extensions with a `code` stub logging and exiting 1 -> exit 0, 43 of 43 calls logged. Rendered install-claude-plugins with a failing `claude` stub -> exit 0, 7 of 7 marketplace-add/plugin-install calls logged (14 total `claude` invocations including the idempotency probes). Rendered configure-raycast with a failing `open` stub -> exit 0, 27 of 27 open calls logged. All four `present tool failing names the item` rows fail at baseline (no site prints an item name); all four `all items succeed prints no failure summary` rows pass (no site prints anything about failures on a clean run); configure-raycast:12-13 prints nothing, so its `absent tool skips clean` row correctly reads fail.

findings.description: PASS on the render/execute separation and the mutation harness. The claude-plugins render measurement reproduces exactly, so the clause's stated reason for rendering under the real $HOME is a true premise, not an inference. `chezmoi execute-template` reads the script body from stdin and its includes/templates from the configured source dir, so copying the test file into a 1dec91c worktree does test the baseline script bodies against unchanged data — which is what makes part 4 discriminating.
findings.evidence: `chezmoi execute-template <run_onchange_after_install-claude-plugins.sh.tmpl` -> 7 lines matching ^(add_marketplace|install_plugin); same command with HOME=/tmp/.../fakehome -> 0, exit 0. Key gate at run_onchange_after_install-claude-plugins.sh.tmpl:62, else branch at :76. Render costs 0.12s, so 15 renders are not a timing risk. tests/licensed-fonts.bats:22 is the execute-template pattern cited and it exists as described; SRC="${BATS_TEST_DIRNAME}/.." is the idiom at tests/licensed-fonts.bats:12 and tests/doctor.bats:13.

findings.description: PASS. Requirement 2 now has a check that can detect its own failing example, which is what r3's blocker demanded: V-1's check part 2 greps for the `status" -eq 0` assertion with a floor of one per @test block and forbids `-ne 0`/`-eq 1`, and the repo's existing bats idiom matches that pattern literally. Combined with V-2's requirement that `bats tests/` exit 0 at HEAD, a worker who makes the scripts exit 1 after collecting failures is caught twice. The claude-plugins description is also now correct: the rendered script is a flat sequence, not a loop.
findings.evidence: tests/doctor.bats:97, :232, :252 all read `[ "$status" -eq 0 ]`, which `grep -c 'status" -eq 0'` matches. Rendered claude-plugins emits `add_marketplace` at lines 43-45 and `install_plugin` at 47-50 with no loop construct. install-packages is correctly exempted from requirement 1: it is a single `brew bundle` invocation at run_onchange_install-packages.sh.tmpl:31.

findings.description: PASS on the push check, which is the part r2 rebuilt. `git rev-list 1dec91c..HEAD` excludes the baseline commit itself, so the fact that 1dec91c is already on origin/main does not produce a false FAIL — the range is empty right now and will contain only the worker's commits.
findings.evidence: `git rev-list 1dec91c..HEAD | wc -l` -> 0 at job start. `git branch -r --contains HEAD` -> `origin/HEAD -> origin/main` and `origin/main`, confirming the mechanism fires on a pushed sha; an unpushed sha prints nothing. Remote `origin` is configured.

findings.description: PASS, and the r3 finding is closed correctly. The before/after `defaults read` probe is gone, replaced by a recording-stub requirement, and the clause's stated reason for that swap is exactly right: the key already holds the value the script writes. The stub requirement is load-bearing rather than decorative — under a scrubbed PATH the raycast script cannot reach the final echo without a `defaults` on PATH, because it runs under set -e. The boltdb probe is also well-founded: `chezmoi execute-template`, which V-1 mandates on every case, does not touch the file.
findings.evidence: `defaults read com.raycast.macos raycastGlobalHotkey` -> `Command-49`, the literal at run_onchange_configure-raycast.sh.tmpl:30. Executing the rendered raycast script under PATH=stubs:/usr/bin:/bin invoked the `defaults` stub exactly once after the 27 open calls. ~/.config/chezmoi/chezmoistate.boltdb mtime is 2026-08-06 20:26:14 and stayed there across five `chezmoi execute-template` runs during this audit. _working-memory/conventions.md:43 already establishes the logging-stub convention the clause leans on.

findings.description: PASS on spec coverage, and r3's stderr under-reach is closed by B-2 requirement 4. AC1 -> B-2.2 + B-1 (with the live apply explicitly deferred to the user); AC2 -> B-2.1 + B-3.2 + V-1's absent-tool cases; AC3 -> B-2.3; AC4 -> B-3.1 + V-1's keeps-going cases; AC5 -> V-3; AC7 -> B-1 + D-1; AC8 -> V-2 + V-1 + D-4. AC6 was independently re-derived once more and remains a sound non-goal; it is not reinstated. Every clause is falsifiable with a describable violating artifact, no two clauses contradict, and Protected content correctly declares no manifest.
findings.evidence: Three of four sites end their install call with 2>/dev/null (vscode:21, raycast:22, claude-plugins:34 and :41); install-packages:31 does not — B-2 requirement 4's premise is exact. The precedent it leans on is real: run_onchange_after_install-global-node-packages.sh.tmpl:34-36 argues for letting stderr through. AC6: dot_local/bin/executable_dotfiles-sync contains no `chezmoi apply` invocation (the three grep hits at :44, :163, :171 are all inside echo/notify strings) and truncates the log at :23 (`: >"$LOG"  # truncate log each run`).

findings.description: One of the five command-keyed greps is inert as written. The Measured baseline table renders the raycast install call as `open "raycast://…"` with a literal Unicode ellipsis, and B-1's check tells a checker-deterministic to substitute the table's command into `grep -nE '<command>.*\|\| (true|echo)'`. That pattern matches nothing at baseline, so it would report clean against an entirely unconverted raycast script. B-1's own stated failing example is still detected (by the four other greps and by the four-paths diff check), and V-1's raycast cases plus V-2's green-suite requirement are a strong backstop, so nothing escapes the constitution as a whole — but the check as literally specified cannot see the site it is aimed at.
findings.evidence: `grep -nE 'open "raycast://…".*\|\| (true|echo)' run_onchange_configure-raycast.sh.tmpl` -> no output, exit 1, at 1dec91c. The same grep keyed to `open` -> `22:  open "raycast://extensions/install/$ext" 2>/dev/null || true`. constitution.md:46 (table cell) and constitution.md:61 (the check).

findings.description: The clause announces `Three requirements, one per case:` and then lists four. Requirement 4 (the reason survives) was appended in this revision without updating the count, which is the patch artifact this revision's approach trades into. The check does cover requirement 4 explicitly, so no requirement is actually lost — but a checker told there are three has a documented licence to stop at three, in a blocker clause whose whole subject is precision about output.
findings.evidence: constitution.md:70 `Three requirements, one per case:` against constitution.md:72-79, which enumerates 1, 2, 3, 4. constitution.md:80 does address requirement 4 in the check.

findings.description: Requirement 4's mechanical FAIL condition is keyed to the literal string `2>/dev/null` and misses the two equivalent spellings. A converted script that writes `code --install-extension "$ext" >/dev/null 2>&1 || failed+=("$ext")` or `&>/dev/null` discards stderr just as thoroughly and matches neither grep. This is a judgment check, so a checker reading the script for whether the reason survives will likely catch it, and the requirement's prose is unambiguous; the stated grep is the weak part, not the requirement. Requirement 4 is also the one requirement with no failing example of its own in the clause's failing-example list.
findings.evidence: constitution.md:80: `For requirement 4, grep -n '2>/dev/null' <each converted script>`. constitution.md:82's two failing examples both illustrate requirements 2 and 3.

findings.description: The structural invariant this revision is built on is very nearly true but not quite: one behavioural requirement about what the scripts print lives outside B-2. `a clean run prints no failure summary` is stated only in V-1's mandated case title and in B-5's check; B-2 says nothing about the clean case, so B-5's claim that an empty summary on a clean run `contradict[s] B-2` overstates what B-2 says. The requirement is well-formed and the system resolves it consistently toward silence (a script printing `Failed: none` would fail the V-1-titled case at HEAD and so fail V-2), but a worker reading the behaviour clauses alone will not find it. Note this is a much smaller version of r3's finding, not a recurrence: B-5's fixture now exists in V-1, and D-4's stub requirement is genuinely a fixture requirement that does not touch the case set.
findings.evidence: constitution.md:13 and constitution.md:70 (`the only clause describing what the scripts print`) against constitution.md:131 (the case title `all items succeed prints no failure summary`) and constitution.md:107-108 (B-5's live-defect text and its output-reading FAIL condition). B-2's requirement list at constitution.md:72-79 contains no clean-run requirement.

findings.description: The fourth deterministic bullet is judgment-shaped work routed to checker-deterministic. Deciding that a `defaults` stub is on PATH `for every case that executes the rendered raycast script` requires per-case reading, not a script invocation — which is precisely the distinction the clause draws two bullets later when it moves the stub-versus-real-call question to checker-judgment `because it is reading comprehension rather than a grep result`. In practice the stub will live in setup() and one grep will settle it, and the judgment bullet is a backstop, so the routing risk is small.
findings.evidence: constitution.md:253 under the checker-deterministic heading at constitution.md:249, against constitution.md:255-256. The requirement itself is load-bearing and correct: under a scrubbed PATH the rendered raycast script runs `defaults write` at :30 under `set -e`, so without a stub the script dies at 127 before its final echo and every raycast case's `status -eq 0` assertion fails.

findings.description: A blocker clause whose named check goes vacuous at the moment D-3 is satisfied, with no FAIL condition stated for the fallback. check-diff-scope.py reads only `git status --porcelain` plus `git diff --name-only`, so once the worker commits and the tree is clean, it reports OK regardless of what the commits touched. The clause anticipates this and hands the checker `git diff --name-only 1dec91c..HEAD` — but D-3, where that command actually appears in a check, enumerates its FAIL conditions (dirty tree, pushed commit, trailer, hard-wrapped body, message that restates the diff) and out-of-scope paths is not among them. The intent is legible enough for a checker to act on, and D-1's clause text still governs; the gap is that neither clause writes down the failing condition for the post-commit form.
findings.evidence: check-diff-scope.py:86-104 (`collect_changed_paths` = status + unstaged diff only) and its docstring at :26-29. constitution.md:213 (D-1's own acknowledgement) against constitution.md:236-238 (D-3's inputs and its FAIL enumeration).
